target: Let u be transcendental over a field K inside C, S a finite set of integers, V_S the K-span of the powers u^s, s in S. Claim: there exist K-independent x_1..x_p and K-independent y_1..y_q in C with all products x_i y_j in V_S if and only if S contains a sumset A+B with |A|=p, |B|=q. Equivalent forms: (1) the rank-one p x q matrix (x_i y_j) has entries in V_S and independent rows and columns; (2) for p=2: some r outside K has dim(V_S cap r V_S) >= q, iff some d != 0 has |S cap (S+d)| >= q; (3) for p=q=2: V_S is a Sidon space (Bachoc-Serra-Zemor) iff S is a Sidon set; (4) geometrically: the monomial curve C_S carries a 1-generic p x q matrix of linear forms of rank one on the curve (p=q=2: a quadric of rank <=4 through C_S), iff A+B is in S. Consequences: {0,±1,±k} has a 2x3 configuration only for k=2,3; for 4<=k<l, {0,±1,±k,±l} has one iff l is in {k+1,k+2,2k-1,2k,2k+1,3k}; {0,±1} together with all ±4^j has none.

leads.citation: C. Bachoc, A. Couvreur, G. Zémor, Towards a function field version of Freiman's Theorem, Algebraic Combinatorics 1 (2018), no. 4, 501-521; arXiv:1709.00087
leads.location: Proposition 3.1 and Lemma 3.2, section 3 (p. 4 of the arXiv version)
leads.quote: The set v(S) is finite and its cardinality equals dim S.
leads.derivation: Only-if direction, all p,q. Rescale: x_i/x_1 and x_1 y_j lie in K(u) with the same products. The u-adic valuation has residue field K, so Prop. 3.1 gives |v(X)|=p, |v(Y)|=q, and multiplicativity gives v(X)+v(Y) inside v(V_S)=S. The converse is trivial. Caveats: the paper states only S and S^2 (the two-space inclusion is my one-line step), states no iff, and contains no sumset-containment statement. This is the valuation method the entry already credits to BSZ17 section 7, in a more citable form, not a printed statement of the theorem. It supports the class 'routine' and does not break 'not found'.

leads.citation: R. M. Roth, N. Raviv, I. Tamo, Construction of Sidon Spaces With Applications to Coding, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 64 (2018), no. 6, 4412-4422; arXiv:1705.04560
leads.location: Construction 21 and Lemma 22, with Lemma 20, Section IV (p. 5 of the arXiv version)
leads.quote: The subspace V ∈ Gq (n, k) from Construction 21 is a max-span Sidon …
leads.derivation: Closest printed statement about spans of powers. Dictionary (my derivation): a space has no 2x2 configuration iff it is a Sidon space, because ab=cd gives x=(a,c), y=(1,d/a). Lemma 22 then says: S a Sidon set in [m], gamma of degree n>2m over F_q, implies span of gamma^s has no 2x2 configuration. That is the p=q=2 only-if direction, in a finite-field setting with gamma algebraic of high degree, not transcendental over a general K. It does not formally imply the target, gives nothing for 2x3, and does not reach the hulls, because {0,±1,±k} is never Sidon (-1+1=0+0).

leads.citation: C. Castello, On generalized Sidon spaces, Linear Algebra Appl. 704 (2024/25), 270-308; arXiv:2312.12245
leads.location: Theorem 4.3, Section 4 (p. 11 of the arXiv version)
leads.quote: then V is a max-span r-Sidon space.
leads.derivation: Extends the Roth-Raviv-Tamo construction: a B_r-set S in [h], gamma of degree n>rh over F_q, gives span of gamma^s r-Sidon. This generalises in r (products of r factors), not in the p x q shape. Same finite-field setting. No statement for a sumset A+B inside S with |A| or |B| at least 3.

leads.citation: S. L'vovsky, On inflection points, monomial curves, and hypersurfaces containing projective curves, Math. Ann. 306 (1996), 719-735; preprint alg-geom/9504002 (On number of hypersurfaces containing projective curves)
leads.location: Proposition 3.1 and its proof, Section 3, p. 3 of the preprint; monomial curves in Section 4
leads.quote: Among m-fold products of sj's there are exactly Spanm(A) that have different orders
leads.derivation: The same inequality in algebraic-geometry vocabulary, on any smooth curve and predating the BSZ/BCZ line: adapted bases at a point give dim Im Sym^m V >= |mA| for A the vanishing sequence. It bounds the size of symmetric products from below. It does not treat a pair X,Y inside a fixed monomial space and has no sumset-containment statement. Method only, independent of the Kneser line.

notes:
**Outcome.** No printed statement of the theorem, in any of the vocabularies tried. "Not found" survives. Run time was about 11 minutes of the 30-minute box (10:23 to 10:34), so this is not exhaustive: I stopped when new query families had stopped yielding candidates.

**The most useful restatements (my own derivations, not from a source).**
- p=2: a 2×q configuration in V exists iff some r∉K has dim(V∩rV) ≥ q. So the target at p=2 reads: max over r∉K of dim(V_S∩rV_S) equals max over d≠0 of |S∩(S+d)|. This is the cyclic orbit code quantity, since d(V,αV)=2k−2dim(V∩αV).
- p=q=2: "no 2×2 configuration" is the same as Sidon space, and "S contains A+B with |A|=|B|=2" is the same as S not being a Sidon set (3-term progressions included). So this case reads: V_S is a Sidon space iff S is a Sidon set.
- Geometry: a configuration is a 1-generic matrix of linear forms of rank one on the monomial curve C_S. For p=q=2 it is a quadric of rank ≤4 through C_S.
- Hankel side: X⊗Y lies in the preimage of V_S under multiplication iff the sparse Hankel matrices supported off S share a p×q zero block, which makes them a compression space. A+B⊂S is a biclique in a Cayley sum graph.

**What each line gave.**
- *Linear Kneser, BCZ line.* BCZ18 Prop. 3.1 is the cleanest citation for |v(X)|=dim X, and the paper calls it classical. With v(xy)=v(x)+v(y) it gives the only-if direction in two lines, so the entry's class "routine" looks right. BCZ18 and Couvreur–Zémor state S² only; I found no two-space v(S)+v(T) inclusion in BSZ17, BCZ18, or Couvreur–Zémor. Their monomial spaces x^a appear only as motivating examples, with S² generated by x^(A+A); they do not ask what products lie inside a given monomial span.
- *Sidon spaces and subspace codes.* This is the only line with statements about spans of powers: Roth–Raviv–Tamo Lemma 22 and Castello Thm 4.3. They go from a Sidon or B_r set to a Sidon-type space, over F_q with γ of large degree, via maximal dim V^r. Neither gives the converse as a stated result, and neither handles an S that fails to be Sidon, which is what the hulls {0,±1,±k} need. I found no statement bounding dim(V∩αV) by the difference multiplicities of a monomial basis beyond the Sidon case. Trautmann et al. use difference multisets over all elements of U, which is a different object.
- *Riemann–Roch, linear series.* L'vovsky Prop. 3.1 is the same valuation inequality under the name vanishing sequence. Elias and Colarte-Gómez–Elias–Miró-Roig relate sumsets to Hilbert functions of monomial curves and Veronese projections, which concerns |sA| only.
- *Determinantal, scrolls.* The rank index papers and Sidman–Smith give the dictionary but no monomial classification. No paper found on scrolls or rank-4 quadrics containing a general monomial curve in terms of exponents.
- *Schanuel, Kirby, Ax.* Nothing relevant. The target is a statement about K(u), with no exponential content.
- *Müntz, Ritt, tropical, group algebra, compression spaces.* Searches produced nothing on point. These were judged from search snippets only and are weak negatives.

**The consequences.** The k=2,3 statement, the pair list and the 4^j statement are finite or elementary sumset checks once the theorem is in hand. No source treating them was found, and I would not expect a printed source outside transcendence work. I spot-checked k=2,3,4 by hand via difference multiplicities, and that agrees with the entry.

**Not settled.**
- zbMATH was unavailable, so MSC-based browsing was not done.
- Castello's 2026 thesis was not read and is the one source most likely to contain a function-field Sidon statement.
- Many items in the screened list were only keyword-searched, not read; a statement phrased without my search terms could be missed.
- All arXiv text was read through pdftotext. The quoted statements read cleanly, but I did not check them against page images.

No repository outside the permitted target file and local sources folder was opened; downloads were kept in a scratch folder and deleted.
